name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: Alaska's statutes have no e-bike category, so an e-bike on public roads falls under the motor-driven cycle: a motorcycle, motor scooter, motorized bicycle or similar conveyance with a motor attached and an engine of 50 cc or less. Defined by Alaska Statutes §28.90.990(a)(22); HB 8, which would have made three-class e-bikes bicycles, passed in 2023 but was vetoed, and no replacement had been enacted by 2026.
restrictions: Not a bicycle under Alaska's traffic rules, which define a bicycle as propelled exclusively by human power
The rider has the rights and duties of a vehicle driver
The rider needs a driver's license; a 14- or 15-year-old may ride with an M2 permit, which takes parental consent, a written motorcycle knowledge test and a vision test
The rider sits astride the permanent seat, facing forward, with both hands on the handlebars
Carries a passenger only on a permanent seat designed for more than one person
Entitled to a full traffic lane, but may not pass in the same lane or ride between lanes of traffic

In state parks, regulations define an electric bicycle as one with fully operable pedals and a motor under 750 watts, in three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph with a motor under 500 watts, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph
In state parks, any class may ride roads open to cars and trails open to off-road vehicles, but only Class 1 may ride trails open to bicycles, unless a trail is posted closed
A state park director may temporarily close a trail or area to e-bikes to protect the land, reduce user conflicts or for safety
